subject: Private VPC pricing - token volumes & licensing (FintechCo)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Hossain <aisha.hossain@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Private VPC pricing & token volumes (recap + next steps)

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap from today
- Use case: customer support automation + transaction summarization (PII redaction required).
- Deployment: Private (VPC) with customer-managed networking; wants on-prem option evaluation later.
- Expected token volumes (initial): rough ballpark mentioned on call: between 100M to 300M tokens/month, with growth to ~500M+ in 12–18 months.
- Latency SLOs: p95 generation latency target ~400–600ms for standard chat flows.

Primary commercial topics to qualify
1) Target unit economics: you mentioned a target of $/1M tokens range — we asked for the target $/1M tokens so we can map to platform + inference costs.
2) Licensing model: options we discussed — (A) Per-seat / user license (not ideal for heavy API usage), (B) Node/GPU-based license + platform fee (common for Private), (C) Hybrid capex + annual support.
3) Support tier: Standard vs Enterprise (Enterprise includes 24x7 on-call, 1-hr P1 SLA, on-site options for on-prem installs).
4) Environment counts: dev/staging/prod + optionally a DR region (helps size licensing and support).

Next steps / asks from us
- Please confirm expected monthly token volume range (low/typical/high) and a target $/1M tokens you’re aiming for.
- Confirm how many environments you expect us to support at go-live (e.g., 1 prod, 1 staging, 2 dev, 1 DR).
- Any procurement timeline / gating items (security questionnaire, SOC 2, contract redlines) we should prioritize.

Deliverables from Redwood
- I’ll send a draft pricing pack with licensing options (attached) and a sample quote with ranges for token-unit economics + license/support breakout.
- Marissa (cc’d) will follow up to propose a technical deep-dive/workshop to scope environment needs.

Proposed short timeline
- Today/Tomorrow: Ben sends pricing pack & initial range estimates (attached).
- Early next week: technical deep-dive w/ Marissa to confirm env count and integration constraints.

If this looks right I’ll send the pricing sheet now.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_Private_Pricing_Pack_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

From: Aisha Hossain <aisha.hossain@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-21T08:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC pricing & token volumes (recap + next steps)

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token volumes: for budgeting purposes please use the following ranges:
  • Low: 100M tokens/month
  • Expected: 200M tokens/month
  • Upside: 400–500M tokens/month within 12 months

- Target $/1M tokens: our finance lead has asked us to aim for $2,500–$4,000 per 1M tokens initially (we understand this depends on batching/quantization and model choice).

- Environments: we expect 4 environments at launch: 1 prod, 1 staging, 1 pre-prod (for legal/regulatory sign-off), 1 dev. We may add a DR environment later.

- Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize commercial terms by end of October. Security/compliance: we’ll need SOC2 report and encryption-at-rest details — procurement will share a questionnaire soon.

Couple quick questions:
1) For Private/VPC licensing, do you price per-GPU or per-environment? Which approach gives us better predictability if we scale from 1→4 nodes?
2) What’s included in Enterprise support vs Standard (response times, on-call coverage, paid on-site visits)?

Can you send the pricing pack and a sample quote that matches the token ranges above? Also loop in anyone on your side who will do the technical sizing.

Thanks —
Aisha
Head of Platform, FintechCo
aisha.hossain@fintechco.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Hossain <aisha.hossain@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tom Garcia <tom.garcia@procure-fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-09-21T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC pricing & token volumes (recap + next steps)

Aisha — appreciate the ranges and timeline. Quick answers below and an initial pricing sketch attached.

Licensing models (summary)
- Node/GPU-based license (recommended for Private): annual license per GPU-node + a fixed platform fee (example: license per A100-equivalent or per 8xA100 cluster unit). Scales predictably as you add nodes.
- Per-environment add-on: small per-environment fee for extra environments (dev/staging) to cover additional deployment templates and snapshot backups.
- Hybrid/capex option: one-time perpetual license + annual support, useful for on-prem commitments.

Support tier differences
- Standard: business-hours email support, 24-hour P1 response target, quarterly reviews.
- Enterprise: 24x7 on-call, 1-hour P1 response SLA, named TAM, quarterly on-site or remote runbooks, prioritized bug fixes (subject to license terms).

Initial pricing sketch (ballpark; final quote to follow)
- Platform fee (annual): $60k–$120k (depends on contract length & features enabled).
- License per GPU-node (annual): $35k–$75k per A100-equivalent node.
- Per-environment add-on: $5k per additional non-prod environment/year.
- Token unit costs (managed inference unit economics, indicative): $2,000–$4,500 per 1M tokens depending on model family, quantization, and batching.

Mapping to your ranges
- At 200M tokens/month (~2.4B tokens/year) target: the unit economics line will dominate run rates; we’ll produce a sample TCO showing token costs + fixed license/support amortized.

Attached: Redwood_Private_Pricing_Pack_v2.pdf (contains a sample quote matrix for 100M / 200M / 500M monthly profiles).

Next steps
- Marissa (cc) will schedule a 60–90min technical deep-dive early next week to confirm exact environment sizing and network constraints.
- I’ll open a formal quote (deal id FT-2027-0922) and share with Procurement.

Anything you want us to include in the technical deep-dive? Examples: model family constraints (LLM size), expected concurrency, preferred GPUs, existing KMS/HSM requirements.

Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_Private_Pricing_Pack_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Hi Aisha — looping in to propose the technical workshop.

Short agenda suggestion (60–90 minutes)
- Infra requirements: expected concurrency, peak QPS, desired p95 latency
- Environment layout: confirm 4 environments + any DR / analytics cluster needs
- Model choices: discuss options (open 7B/13B vs larger LLMs) and expected memory/kv-cache sizing
- Network & security: VPC peering, egress control, KMS integrations, SOC2 evidence checklist
- Deliverables: finalized environment count, recommended GPU count by environment, and a draft bill-of-materials for quote.

Availability: Wed/Thu next week 10:00–12:00 PT works for our infra team. Please confirm which slot you prefer and who from your engineering/procurement teams will attend.

I’ll prepare a preliminary sizing worksheet and bring our solutions engineer.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
